title: Learning
content: What Is Learning? Learning is the acquisition of knowledge and skills. All new learning requires a foundation of prior knowledge, so in some way, learning is an iterative process that relies on making connections to existing knowledge and experiences. Learning is better when it is harder, for it yields better mastery of the topic and longer retention compared to when it's made "easy". The book Make It Stick talks in depth about learning and is where most of the concepts in this and related notes originate from. You learn better when you go wide (i.e. BFS), drawing on all of your aptitudes and resourcefulness Learning Building Blocks All forms and practices of learning are built atop one or more of the following concepts, hence them being coined building blocks. Encoding Consolidation Retrieval Practice Generation effect Elaboration Spaced repetition Abstraction These building blocks are incorporated into Learning patterns that reliably lead to long lasting learning. Note that there are Learning anti-patterns that degrade the learning experience and yield subpar results given the time it takes to execute on them. How Learning Occurs The learning process roughly follows these steps: Encoding - the process of converting sensory perceptions into mental representations of observed patterns called memory traces Consolidation - the process of strengthening memory traces and storing them in long term memory Retrieval - the act of remembering memory traces stored in long term memory For learning to be durable, in addition to the step-by-step process described prior, one needs to associate the new material with a diverse set of cues that will help in recalling that knowledge. This is often done in the form of relating to prior knowledge (hence why new learning requires prior knowledge). [!info] This is self-aggrandizing but I was able to do this instinctively when I was younger (was I a savant like that?) Knowledge, skills, and experiences that are vivid and hold significance, and those that are periodically practiced, stay with us. What Does It Take To Learn? Retrieval for the sake of learning Reflection is a form of practice Testing Effect Exploring Nuances The greater the effort to retrieve learning, provided that you succeed, the more that learning is strengthened by retrieval. Giving students corrective feedback after tests keeps them from incorrectly retaining material they have misunderstood and produces better learning of the correct answers Adding Variety TBD Embracing Difficulty When learning is difficult it yields better understanding and remembering. One should embrace the difficulties that come with learning and be patient with how apparently "slow" the learning becomes compared to other methods that seem easy but give you an Illusion of mastery. That learning will yield results in the short term that seem very desirable but in actuality, does not last long. The old adage To go fast, first go slow applies here. Difficulty forces us to slow down and truly internalize what is being learned or trained (e.g. Mia Blundetto's PLF practice). Rather than having an illusion of master, it's best to have Confidence based on repeated performance. And that can be achieved by learning with an embrace for the difficulty that comes with it. However, not all difficulty in learning is the same. There's desirable and undesirable difficulties Desirable Difficulties These are short-term impediments that are favorable for long-term learning. Reconsolidation of Memory During a focused, effortful recall, the learning is made pliable again: the most salient aspects of it become clearer, and the consequent reconsolidation helps to reinforce meaning, strengthen connections to prior knowledge, bolster the cues and retrieval routes for recalling it later, and weaken competing routes. Creation of Mental Models Mental Models are forms of deeply entrenched and highly efficient skills or knowledge structures that, like habits, can be adapted and applied in varied circumstances. And doing these is rather hard but it provides significant benefits in the long run. Variability Retrieval difficulties posed by spacing, interleaving, and variation are overcome by invoking the same mental processes that will be needed when applying the learning to practice. [!quote] Practice like you play, and you'll play like you practice. [!quote] The only thing that won't betray you is your training History's Strongest Disciple Kenichi [!quote] Not everyone who works hard is rewarded. But, all those who succeeded have worked hard Hajime No Ippo Related Notes building a plane while in mid-air Work-life balance feels like a myth if your goal is to get ahead Conceptual Learning

title: All new learning requires a foundation of prior knowledge
content:
Having knowledge is necessary for long term learning for without knowledge, you don't have the foundation for the higher level skills of analysis, synthesis, and creative problem solving.

[!quote] One cannot apply what one knows in a practical manner if one does not know anything to apply.

Mastery requires both the possession of ready knowledge ad the conceptual understanding of how to use it.

Because learning is based on prior knowledge, the more we learn, the more possible connections we create for learning, i.e. the more we learn the more are able to learn.
